Common causes of gaps in sugarcane germination, a planting checklist and the planting program with Immunity Granules and Sugarcane Special.
Why germination gaps appear in sugarcane
Home › Blog › Why germination gaps appear in sugarcane
If germination is not even after planting, the crop stand of the whole field suffers. Gaps mean replanting, which adds both cost and time.
Common causes of germination gaps
Sett quality: old, dried-out or diseased setts do not sprout well from their buds.
Moisture: too little or too much soil moisture at planting can affect germination.
Depth and soil pressure: setts placed too deep or too shallow germinate unevenly.
Soil condition: a hard pan, salinity or poor drainage can affect the root zone.
Soil-borne pests and diseases: setts and the root zone are at risk of damage.
Planting checklist
Choose healthy, fresh setts.
Keep the right soil moisture at planting.
Place setts at an even depth and cover them with soil properly.
Apply Granules at planting itself, for the root zone.
Note down the dates of the first irrigation and the herbicide application.

Why sugarcane tillers / canes die
Home › Blog › Why sugarcane tillers / canes die
Many farmers complain that the cane starts well but later the tillers / canes die. This lowers the plant population and can finally affect the yield.
Common causes of tiller death
Water stress: a shortage of water, or water standing in the field.
Nutrient imbalance: not getting the right nutrition at the right time.
Crowding and shade: late tillers cannot survive against bigger plants.
Pests and diseases: damage at the early stage.
Early stress: if germination and early growth are weak, the effect shows later.
Stage-wise care
Instead of doing everything at once, work stage by stage: Granules at planting, drenching after the first irrigation, and a foliar spray at 2–4 leaves.
2–4 leaves: 250 ML Sugarcane Special + 250 ML Immunity Gold / vigha4–5 pumps per vigha (45–50 ML in every 15-litre pump).
Repeat spray: every 15–25 days2–3 further sprays depending on crop condition.
Alongside, continue the program with 1 bag of Granules at every main fertilizer dose.

Shri Vishalkumar Satishbhai Patel, a progressive farmer from Ashtagam in Navsari (Gujarat), grows the 707 variety of sugarcane. What follows is in his own words.
His experience (as he describes it)
He started a treatment program with Immunity Sugarcane Special, Immunity Granules and Immunity Gold.
He reports seeing germination of around 95–100%.
He reports mortality of close to zero.
He reports a 30–40% reduction in chemical costs.
He reports yield rising from 30–35 tonnes to 45 tonnes.
Important:This is one farmer's personal experience, not a product promise or guarantee. Results can differ with soil, water, variety, weather and farm management.
